Isaiah

Introduction

Isayas the child of Amus (was) the (one who) wrote this document (LIT reading). He (was) one prophet of God, and he lived there in Hirusalim. The meaning of the name ‘Isayas’, (is) ‘The Lord God (is) the (one who) Saves.’ This document (LIT reading) was_written about 740 up_to 680 years before Hisus was_born. And it's divided into three portions:

1/ Chapter(s) 1–39: It's storied here concerning the time that Asirya was_threatening Huda, the kingdom there in the south (LIT right side). And Isayas saw that due [surprise] to the sin of the people, to their disobedience, and to lack of their trusting in God, (was) the reason why Huda was_threatened by Asirya. Isayas carefully taught the people and their leaders to_live with right actions and (to have) correct judging. He warned them that if they don't listen to the word of God, they would_ indeed _be_destroyed. But Isayas also prophesied the birth of the descendant of Dabid in the future that's worthy to_be_followed by the people, and the time would_arrive that the entire world will have peace.

2/ Chapters 40–55: It's prophesied here concerning the future capturing and carrying of many people of Huda there going_to Babilunya. The prophet Isayas informed that even so, the people should not get_weak and lose hope because God would rescue his people and would return them there to Hirusalim in_order to_begin new living. The theme of these chapters, God (is) the (one who) determines what_will_happen and the (one who) plans for his people, and included also in this purpose of_theirs there to all nations is_to_receive blessing from God by_means of Israil.

3/ Kapitulu 56–66: It's also prophesied here concerning the living of the people that God would return there to Hirusalim. Isayas tells here the commands of God concerning righteous living, correct judging, obeying the Day of Resting, sacrificing, and praying. And it can_be_read in these chapters the word that was_used by Hisus for informing that he was_chosen in_order for preaching the good story (Isaiah 61:1-2; Luke 4:18-19).
